title: Day 29 · Week 4, Day 1 — Brain: the primitive streak, the seam that becomes a spine, and the four hundred micrograms
summary: The first Brain episode, on a day when there is no brain yet — only a line. The primitive streak forms along the 0.2 mm embryonic disc at Carnegie stage 6, fixing head, tail, left and right; gastrulation sorts cells into endoderm, mesoderm and the ectoderm that becomes skin and the whole nervous system; the notochord induces the neural plate around Day 32–33; the neural folds begin to fuse around Day 36 from two (or three) sites and the neuropores seal by about Day 40–42, before the first appointment. What happens when they don't: spina bifida (1 in 2,857 US births) and anencephaly, ~3,000 affected US pregnancies a year. The folic acid evidence in full — the MRC Vitamin Study (1,817 women, 72% reduction), Czeizel & Dudás (4,753 women, 0 vs 6), the Cochrane review (7,391 women, RR 0.31, high quality, 400 µg is enough), fortification (~1,326 births a year spared) and the USPSTF 2023 Grade A — plus the 4 mg exception and why starting today still counts. Then the two brain nutrients prenatal vitamins often skip: iodine (the embryo depends entirely on the mother's thyroxine until ~Day 84; ALSPAC verbal-IQ odds 1.58; only 34 of 59 US prenatals contain any; the trials are low quality) and choline (90–95% of pregnant women below 450 mg; the 26-woman Caudill trial, emerging). And the honest answer on the two weeks before the test: the all-or-none period, the CDC's 'stop now' line, and the ABCD cohort's children exposed only before maternal knowledge who did not differ from the unexposed.
action: Tonight, turn the prenatal bottle around and read two lines. Folic acid/folate: at least 400 µg (667 µg DFE is the same thing). Iodine: on the label at all, ideally 150 µg. If both are there, you are done. If iodine is missing, add 'prenatal has no iodine — what should we do?' to the question list for the first visit and make sure the kitchen salt is iodized. The full label walkthrough is Day 33.
